lift-station_test.yaml:
# Acceptance tests for the lift station's control narrative — no Go, no
# toolchain, run on the bench manifest (nautilus.yaml) in virtual time.
#
#   naut test              run them
#   naut test -v           with virtual elapsed time per test
#   naut test -run "storm"  only tests whose name matches
#
# File-level suspend: [sim] below is the default for every test — driving
# the process values directly is how an open-loop test gets an exact,
# repeatable answer out of closed-loop control logic. A test only states
# its own `suspend:` when it needs something OTHER than that default (an
# empty `suspend: []` to run the sim closed-loop, or an extra task
# suspended alongside it) — Test.Suspend REPLACES the file's list rather
# than adding to it, so such a test must repeat `sim` itself.
tolerance: 0.5
suspend: [sim]

tests:
  - name: lead pump starts at LeadOn and post-runs after LeadOff
    given: { LIT101_Level: 65.0, P101_Running: true } # RunFb, so the starter doesn't fail-to-run
    steps:
      - advance: 1s
        expect: { P101_RunCmd: true, LeadIsP101: true }
      - given: { LIT101_Level: 25.0 } # below LeadOffLevel (30) — PostRun, still running
        advance: 1s
        expect: { P101_RunCmd: true }
      - advance: 21s # PostRunSec (20 s) elapses — pump drops, duty alternates
        expect: { P101_RunCmd: false, LeadIsP101: false }

  - name: lag joins at LagOn and drops at LagOff
    given: { LIT101_Level: 65.0, P101_Running: true, P102_Running: true }
    steps:
      - advance: 1s
        expect: { P101_RunCmd: true, P102_RunCmd: false }
      - given: { LIT101_Level: 85.0 } # above LagOnLevel (80)
        advance: 1s
        expect: { P101_RunCmd: true, P102_RunCmd: true }
      - given: { LIT101_Level: 50.0 } # below LagOffLevel (55), still above LeadOffLevel
        advance: 1s
        expect: { P101_RunCmd: true, P102_RunCmd: false }

  - name: duty alternates every completed cycle
    steps:
      - given: { LIT101_Level: 65.0, P101_Running: true }
        advance: 1s
        expect: { P101_RunCmd: true, P102_RunCmd: false, LeadIsP101: true }
      - given: { LIT101_Level: 25.0 }
        advance: 22s # through PostRun and Alternate, back to Idle
        expect: { CycleCount: 1, LeadIsP101: false }
      - given: { LIT101_Level: 65.0, P102_Running: true } # second cycle: P102 is lead now
        advance: 1s
        expect: { P101_RunCmd: false, P102_RunCmd: true, CycleCount: 2 }

  - name: failover on fail-to-run — the standby takes the call and the fault latches an alarm
    given: { LIT101_Level: 65.0 } # P101_Running left false: never confirms it started
    steps:
      - advance: 5.5s # 5 s fail-to-run timer plus settling
        expect: { P101_FailToRun: true, P102_RunCmd: true }
        alarms: { active: ["P101_FailToRun"] }
      - given: { ResetFaults: true }
        advance: 200ms
        expect: { P101_FailToRun: false }

  - name: three fail-to-run trips lock the pump out, and a reset clears it
    # A direct continuation of the failover test above: keep P101 as lead
    # for all three trips by re-asserting LeadIsP101 after every reset —
    # [main] (sequence.sfc) stays active (unlike the other open-loop
    # tests here) because its own Failover/SwapDuty would otherwise hand
    # the lead to P102 after the very first trip, same as the failover
    # test above; re-given each time it fires, LeadIsP101 sticks until the
    # next trip flips it again.
    given: { LIT101_Level: 65.0, LeadIsP101: true } # P101_Running left false throughout
    steps:
      - advance: 5.7s # trip 1: 5 s fail-to-run timer plus settling
        expect: { P101_FailToRun: true, P101_LockedOut: false }
      - advance: 300ms # let the alarm evaluator catch up to the tag
        alarms: { active: ["P101_FailToRun"] }
      - given: { ResetFaults: true, LeadIsP101: true }
        advance: 200ms
        expect: { P101_FailToRun: false, P101_LockedOut: false }
      - given: { ResetFaults: false, LeadIsP101: true }
        advance: 5.7s # trip 2 — an ordinary Reset-and-retry, same as the failover test's
        expect: { P101_FailToRun: true, P101_LockedOut: false }
      - given: { ResetFaults: true, LeadIsP101: true }
        advance: 200ms
        expect: { P101_FailToRun: false, P101_LockedOut: false }
      - given: { ResetFaults: false, LeadIsP101: true }
        advance: 5.7s # trip 3 — the third trip latches LockedOut
        expect: { P101_FailToRun: true, P101_LockedOut: true, P101_Avail: false }
      - advance: 300ms # let the alarm evaluator catch up to the tags
        alarms: { active: ["P101_FailToRun", "P101_LockedOut"] }
      - given: { ResetFaults: true } # only now does Reset also clear the trip count —
        advance: 200ms                # see lib/motor.ld's `lockout` rung for why
        expect: { P101_FailToRun: false, P101_LockedOut: false }

  - name: the high-high float runs both pumps unless HOA is Off, and alarms critical
    given: { LSHH101: true, P101_Mode: 0, P102_Running: true } # Off wins over the float
    steps:
      - advance: 2.5s
        expect: { P101_RunCmd: false, P102_RunCmd: true }
        alarms: { active: ["LSHH101"] }
      - ack: { ids: ["LSHH101"], by: test }
        scans: 1
        alarms: { state: { LSHH101: ack-active } }
      - given: { LSHH101: false }
        advance: 2.5s
        alarms: { active: [], state: { LSHH101: normal } }

  - name: a seal fail on the lead hands the call to the standby at once
    # A seal fail blocks the lead pump's permissive, so it is not fit to
    # lead (P101_DutyOk false): the sequence gives the lead to P-102 before
    # the call (or fails over to it, if the call came first) instead of
    # waiting for the level to reach LagOn.
    given: { LIT101_Level: 65.0, P101_SealFail: true, P102_Running: true }
    advance: 1s
    expect: { P101_Permissive: false, P101_RunCmd: false, LeadIsP101: false, P102_RunCmd: true }

  - name: LeadSelect holds P-102 as lead across a pump-down
    given: { LeadSelect: 2, LIT101_Level: 65.0, P102_Running: true }
    steps:
      - advance: 1s
        expect: { LeadIsP101: false, P102_RunCmd: true, P101_RunCmd: false }
      - given: { LIT101_Level: 25.0 } # below LeadOff: post-run, then Alternate swaps...
        advance: 22s
        expect: { P102_RunCmd: false }
      - advance: 1s # ...and back in Idle the selection takes the lead again
        expect: { LeadIsP101: false }

  - name: LeadSelect alternate swaps the lead after each pump-down
    given: { LeadSelect: 0, LeadIsP101: true, LIT101_Level: 65.0, P101_Running: true }
    steps:
      - advance: 1s
        expect: { P101_RunCmd: true }
      - given: { LIT101_Level: 25.0 }
        advance: 23s
        expect: { LeadIsP101: false }

  - name: a lead in Off hands the lead over while idle, whatever LeadSelect says
    given: { LeadSelect: 1, P101_Mode: 0, LIT101_Level: 40.0 } # idle: below LeadOn
    steps:
      - advance: 1s
        expect: { LeadIsP101: false } # P-101 selected, but Off: P-102 leads
      - given: { LIT101_Level: 65.0, P102_Running: true }
        advance: 1s
        expect: { P102_RunCmd: true, P101_RunCmd: false }
      - given: { P101_Mode: 2, LIT101_Level: 25.0, P102_Running: false }
        advance: 23s # pump-down done; P-101 is back in Auto
        expect: { LeadIsP101: true } # the selection holds again

  - name: a lead switched to Off mid-cycle fails over to the other pump
    given: { LIT101_Level: 65.0, LeadIsP101: true, P101_Running: true }
    steps:
      - advance: 1s
        expect: { P101_RunCmd: true, LeadIsP101: true }
      - given: { P101_Mode: 0, P101_Running: false, P102_Running: true }
        advance: 1s
        expect: { P101_RunCmd: false, LeadIsP101: false, P102_RunCmd: true }

  - name: a low-low float blocks the lead's permissive, same as a seal fail
    # permissives.ld's p101perm rung ANDs in /LSLL101 — a dry well blocks
    # BOTH pumps, not just the lead, so P102's permissive drops too even
    # though nothing else is wrong with it.
    given: { LIT101_Level: 65.0, LSLL101: true }
    steps:
      - advance: 1s
        expect: { P101_Permissive: false, P102_Permissive: false, P101_RunCmd: false }

  - name: a VFD fault blocks the lead's permissive, same as a seal fail
    given: { LIT101_Level: 65.0, P101_VfdFault: true }
    steps:
      - advance: 1s
        expect: { P101_Permissive: false, P101_RunCmd: false }
      - advance: 500ms # P101_VfdFault's 1 s on-delay
        alarms: { active: ["P101_VfdFault"] }

  - name: hand mode runs each pump at its own hand speed regardless of level
    given: { P101_Mode: 1, P102_Mode: 1, P101_HandSpeedHz: 40.0, P102_HandSpeedHz: 52.0, LIT101_Level: 10.0 } # well below LeadOnLevel
    advance: 1s
    expect:
      - P101_RunCmd: true
      - P101_SpeedCmd: { near: 40.0, tol: 0.5 }
      - P102_RunCmd: true
      - P102_SpeedCmd: { near: 52.0, tol: 0.5 }

  - name: the level PID raises speed above setpoint and lowers it below
    suspend: [sim, main] # drive LeadReq and the level directly; the first
                         # task (sequence.sfc, unnamed in the manifest) is
                         # always the runtime's "main" task regardless —
                         # see nautilus.yaml's first task comment
    given: { LeadReq: true }
    steps:
      - given: { LIT101_Level: 55.0 } # above LevelSP (45): direct-acting, speed climbs
        advance: 25s
        expect: { SpeedRef: { gt: 40.0 } }
      - given: { LIT101_Level: 35.0 } # below LevelSP: speed backs down toward the floor
        advance: 60s
        expect: { SpeedRef: { near: 30.0, tol: 2.0 } }

  - name: the high-level alarm latches at 90% and clears only at or below 85%
    # level.fbd's seal-in: above/below straddle a 5-point hysteresis band
    # around HighLevelAlmSP (90). Without the hysteresis, a naive
    # `HighLevelAlm := GE(Level, 90)` would already read false once the
    # level ticks back down from 90 to 87 — this proves the seal-in holds
    # through that band and only releases at the 85 floor.
    given: { LIT101_Level: 60.0 }
    steps:
      - advance: 1s
        expect: { HighLevelAlm: false }
      - given: { LIT101_Level: 90.0 } # at HighLevelAlmSP — latches
        advance: 1s
        expect: { HighLevelAlm: true }
      - given: { LIT101_Level: 87.0 } # inside the hysteresis band — still on
        advance: 1s
        expect: { HighLevelAlm: true }
      - given: { LIT101_Level: 85.0 } # at the hysteresis floor — clears
        advance: 1s
        expect: { HighLevelAlm: false }

  - name: stats.st accumulates runtime, starts, and station flow
    suspend: [sim, main, level, permissives] # only stats.st runs; drive its
                                              # inputs directly
    given: { P101_Running: false, FIT101_Flow: 160.0 }
    steps:
      - given: { P101_Running: true } # rising edge — one start
        advance: 1s
        expect: { P101_Stats.Starts: 1 }
      - advance: 3600s # about an hour running
        expect:
          - P101_Stats.Starts: 1 # no further starts while it just keeps running
          - P101_Stats.Hours: { near: 1.0, tol: 0.05 }
          - StationFlowGal: { near: 9600.0, tol: 500.0 } # 160 gpm * ~3601 s / 60

  - name: closed loop rides out a storm inflow and settles once it passes
    suspend: [] # override the file default: the sim runs, closed loop
    given: { LIT101_Level: 45.0, InflowGpm: 640.0 } # a storm from mid-level
    steps:
      - advance: 300s
        expect:
          LIT101_Level: { lt: 90.0 }
          CycleCount: { ge: 1 }
      - given: { InflowGpm: 30.0 } # the storm passes; a quiet night flow.
        # (Below MinSpeedHz's ~57 gpm floor on purpose: at or above that
        # floor the level PID just finds a new equilibrium near LevelSP and
        # idles the pump there forever, which is correct variable-speed
        # behavior but means the "storm passes" test needs an inflow the
        # minimum speed can outrun, or a full stop is never reached.)
        until: 900s
        expect: { P101_RunCmd: false, P102_RunCmd: false }

  - name: a pump in Hand pumps the well to low-low once, then is held off until it refills
    # What used to chatter: Hand ran the well down to LSLL, the trip
    # stopped the pump, the float cleared a moment later, the pump started
    # again, every few seconds. Now the trip latches DryRunHold, which
    # holds both pumps off past the float's reset until Lead off.
    suspend: [] # the sim runs: the level falls and refills for real
    given: { P101_Mode: 1, LIT101_Level: 20.0, InflowGpm: 60.0 } # a quiet night: the pump outruns it
    steps:
      - until: 180s
        expect: { LSLL101: true } # pumped down to low-low
      - advance: 1s
        expect: { DryRunHold: true, P101_RunCmd: false }
      - until: 180s
        expect: { LSLL101: false } # the float resets at 12 %...
      - advance: 1s
        expect: { DryRunHold: true, P101_RunCmd: false } # ...but the pump stays held
      - until: 600s
        expect: { DryRunHold: false } # refilled to Lead off (30 %)
      - advance: 2s
        expect: { P101_RunCmd: true } # Hand runs it again

  - name: a shelved high-level alarm is silent and always expires
    # Drives the level, not HighLevelAlm itself — level is left running
    # (only permissives is suspended beyond the file default, sim), so
    # this exercises the same hysteresis seal-in as the test above rather
    # than bypassing it. main must stay unsuspended too: the alarm engine
    # only re-evaluates on the main task's own scan (see runtime.OnScan).
    suspend: [sim, permissives]
    given: { LIT101_Level: 95.0 } # above HighLevelAlmSP (90)
    steps:
      - advance: 11s # past the 10 s on-delay
        alarms: { active: ["HighLevel"] }
      - shelve: { id: HighLevel, for: 15m, by: test }
        scans: 1
        alarms: { shelved: ["HighLevel"], active: [] }
      - advance: 16m
        alarms: { shelved: [], active: ["HighLevel"] }
field.yaml:
# lift-station — the field build: the same duty/standby lead-lag control
# (sequence.sfc, level.fbd, permissives.ld, stats.st — byte-identical to
# nautilus.yaml's) pointed at real VFDs and a remote-I/O rack over Modbus
# TCP instead of the bench's simulated plant. No sim task; the field is
# the field.
#
#   naut modbus serve --manifest modbus_manifest.yaml --values seed.json
#                                         stand in for the devices
#   naut check -m field.yaml .           validate offline
#   naut run   -m field.yaml .           poll them for real
#
# tags/modbus.yaml is GENERATED from devices.yaml by
# `naut modbus import --map devices.yaml` — never hand-edit it, re-run the
# import instead. The importer names every tag `<instance id>_<register
# tag>`, which lands exactly on this project's tag model for both VFDs
# (P101_Running, P101_RunCmd, P101_SpeedCmd, ...) but not for the RIO
# instance (LIT101_Level, LSHH101, ... aren't spellable as `RIO_<...>`).
# field_map.st — the one program that only exists in this manifest — is
# the glue that renames the RIO_* points onto the canonical tags every
# other program reads. See docs/design/examples-dogfood.md for the finding
# and devices.yaml's own header for the naming rule.
name: lift-station

server:
  addr: "localhost:8080"
  online-edits: true
  # Same operator screen as nautilus.yaml — see its comment and the
  # README's "The operator screen" section.
  hmi: hmi/build

retain:
  file: retain.json

tasks:
  - program: field_map.st   # RIO_* -> the canonical tag names, ahead of
    scan: 100ms             # everything else; the first task is always
                            # the runtime's "main" task, whatever it's
                            # called here — naming it (a name: key) is a
                            # no-op `naut check` warns on
  - name: sequence
    program: sequence.sfc
    scan: 250ms
  - name: level
    program: level.fbd
    scan: 100ms
    dt-tag: LevelDtS
  - name: permissives
    program: permissives.ld
    scan: 100ms
  - name: stats
    program: stats.st
    scan: 1s
    dt-tag: StatsDtS

# tags/modbus.yaml supplies the VFD points under their canonical names
# already (P101_Running, P101_RunCmd, P101_SpeedCmd, P101_SpeedHz,
# P101_Amps, P101_VfdFault, and the P102_ twins) plus the RIO points under
# their RIO_ prefix (RIO_Level, RIO_Flow, RIO_LSHH101, RIO_LSLL101,
# RIO_P101_SealFail, RIO_P101_OverTemp, RIO_P102_SealFail,
# RIO_P102_OverTemp). tags/station.yaml supplies every operator setpoint
# and computed-state tag that's byte-identical to nautilus.yaml's — the
# tags: list below keeps only the canonical process values field_map.st
# writes (the field's role: state twin of the bench's sim-owned ones).
tag-files:
  - tags/modbus.yaml
  - tags/station.yaml

tags:
  # The canonical process values field_map.st writes from the RIO_* inputs.
  - { name: LIT101_Level, role: state, init: 0.0, unit: "%", desc: "Wet-well level (LIT-101)" }
  - { name: LSHH101,      role: state, init: false, desc: "High-high float (LSHH-101)" }
  - { name: LSLL101,      role: state, init: false, desc: "Low-low float (LSLL-101)" }
  - { name: FIT101_Flow,  role: state, init: 0.0, unit: "gpm", desc: "Discharge flow (FIT-101)" }
  - { name: P101_SealFail, role: state, init: false, desc: "P-101 seal-leak probe" }
  - { name: P102_SealFail, role: state, init: false, desc: "P-102 seal-leak probe" }
  - { name: P101_OverTemp, role: state, init: false, desc: "P-101 motor over-temperature" }
  - { name: P102_OverTemp, role: state, init: false, desc: "P-102 motor over-temperature" }

  # Operator setpoints and computed state both live in tags/station.yaml
  # (byte-identical to nautilus.yaml's — see its header).

alarms:
  defaults: { ack-required: true, auto-clear: true, shelve: true }
  shelve-times: [15m, 1h, 4h]
  journal: { keep: 500 }
  defs:
    - { id: LSHH101, tag: LSHH101, name: "Wet-well high-high (LSHH-101)", priority: critical, on-delay: 2s, class: process }
    - { id: HighLevel, tag: HighLevelAlm, name: "Wet-well high level (LIT-101)", priority: high, on-delay: 10s, class: process }
    - { id: LSLL101, tag: LSLL101, name: "Wet-well low-low (LSLL-101)", priority: medium, on-delay: 5s, class: process }
    - { id: P101_FailToRun, tag: P101_FailToRun, name: "P-101 failed to run", priority: high, class: equipment }
    - { id: P102_FailToRun, tag: P102_FailToRun, name: "P-102 failed to run", priority: high, class: equipment }
    - { id: P101_LockedOut, tag: P101_LockedOut, name: "P-101 locked out (3 fail-to-run trips)", priority: high, class: equipment }
    - { id: P102_LockedOut, tag: P102_LockedOut, name: "P-102 locked out (3 fail-to-run trips)", priority: high, class: equipment }
    - { id: P101_VfdFault, tag: P101_VfdFault, name: "P-101 VFD fault", priority: high, on-delay: 1s, class: equipment }
    - { id: P102_VfdFault, tag: P102_VfdFault, name: "P-102 VFD fault", priority: high, on-delay: 1s, class: equipment }
    - { id: P101_SealFail, tag: P101_SealFail, name: "P-101 seal-leak probe", priority: medium, on-delay: 5s, class: equipment }
    - { id: P102_SealFail, tag: P102_SealFail, name: "P-102 seal-leak probe", priority: medium, on-delay: 5s, class: equipment }
    - { id: P101_OverTemp, tag: P101_OverTemp, name: "P-101 motor over-temperature", priority: high, on-delay: 2s, class: equipment }
    - { id: P102_OverTemp, tag: P102_OverTemp, name: "P-102 motor over-temperature", priority: high, on-delay: 2s, class: equipment }
    - { id: BothUnavail, tag: BothUnavail, name: "Both pumps unavailable", priority: critical, on-delay: 5s, class: equipment }

driver:
  type: modbus
  manifest: modbus_manifest.yaml
  scan-rate: 500ms
  scan-classes: { fast: 200ms, slow: 2s }
lib/motor.ld:
(* Motor starter library: HOA (Off/Hand/Auto) selection, fail-to-run
   supervision, and a lockout on repeated fail-to-run trips — one block,
   instantiated once per pump in permissives.ld. Written as rungs (docs/functions.md "Function
   blocks in ladder"); a .ld file with no PROGRAM is a project library,
   exactly like a PROGRAM-less .st file. *)

FUNCTION_BLOCK MotorStarter
VAR_INPUT
    Mode       : INT;  (* 0 Off, 1 Hand, 2 Auto *)
    AutoReq    : BOOL; (* called by the sequence/HH override; meaningful in Auto *)
    Permissive : BOOL; (* seal / over-temp / VFD fault / LSLL all clear *)
    RunFb      : BOOL; (* VFD running feedback *)
    Reset      : BOOL; (* pulse: always clears FailToRun; clears the trip count/LockedOut too, but only once LockedOut is actually latched — see the lockout rung below *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    Run       : BOOL;
    InHand    : BOOL;
    FailToRun : BOOL;
    LockedOut : BOOL; (* three fail-to-run trips since the last Reset *)
END_VAR
VAR
    t1 : TON; (* fail-to-run: commanded but not confirmed running for 5 s *)
    c1 : CTU; (* counts FailToRun trips; three latches LockedOut until Reset *)
END_VAR
LD
  RUNG run (* Auto only calls when the sequence/HH override asks; Hand always runs *)
    [ EQ(Mode, 2) AutoReq | EQ(Mode, 1) ] Permissive /FailToRun /LockedOut ( Run )

  RUNG fail (* commanded to run, no running feedback for 5 s: failed to start *)
    Run /RunFb t1:TON(PT := T#5S) ( S FailToRun )

  RUNG reset (* the operator's Reset pulse clears a fail-to-run trip so the pump can retry *)
    Reset ( R FailToRun )

  RUNG hand (* reported back so the speed logic uses the hand speed, not the loop *)
    EQ(Mode, 1) ( InHand )

  // one CTU count per fail-to-run trip; three locks the pump out. The
  // counter's own reset is Reset AND LockedOut, not Reset alone: every
  // ordinary fail-to-run retry pulses Reset just to clear FailToRun and
  // try again, and if that same pulse also zeroed the trip count, three
  // trips could never accumulate — the count would always be back to 0
  // before the next attempt even starts (see docs/design/examples-
  // dogfood.md for the failed-3-trips test that caught this). Gating the
  // counter's reset on LockedOut itself means it only clears once the
  // lockout has actually latched, which is also the one time "clears on
  // Reset" needs to be true.
  RUNG lockout
    +FailToRun c1:CTU(R := AND(Reset, LockedOut), PV := 3, Q => LockedOut)
END_LD
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK
lib/physics.st:
(* Bench-only plant model: a wet-well level integrator and a submersible
   pump/VFD dynamic model. Two FUNCTION_BLOCKs, no PROGRAM — a project
   library (docs/functions.md "A .ld library", the same rule for .st).
   sim.st is the only caller; field.yaml has no sim task, so these two
   blocks sit compiled but unused in that manifest — harmless dead code,
   the same way a project's other library functions are. *)

FUNCTION_BLOCK WetWellModel
(* Integrates a level from an inflow/outflow balance. WW-101: a 13 ft
   level span over 1,320 gal of usable volume between the span's limits,
   so 13.2 gal per %: 100 gpm net moves the level 1 % in about 8 s. *)
VAR_INPUT
    InflowGpm  : REAL;
    OutflowGpm : REAL;
    Dt         : REAL; (* seconds *)
END_VAR
VAR_IN_OUT
    Level : REAL; (* %, 0..100 *)
END_VAR
VAR CONSTANT
    GalPerPercent : REAL := 13.2; (* 1,320 gal span / 100 % = 13.2 gal per % *)
END_VAR
(* gal/min * s / 60 = gal *)
Level := LIMIT(0.0, Level + (InflowGpm - OutflowGpm) * Dt / 60.0 / GalPerPercent, 100.0);
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK

FUNCTION_BLOCK VfdModel
(* A submersible pump + VFD, standing in for the field device on the
   bench: RunCmd/SpeedCmd in, Running/SpeedHz/Amps/Fault out. Running lags
   RunCmd by 0.5 s (starter contactor + soft-start), and drops the instant
   a fault is injected. SpeedHz ramps toward SpeedCmd at 10 Hz/s while
   commanded and running, and ramps back to 0 otherwise. Amps follows
   speed-squared, the affinity-law shape a centrifugal load actually
   draws. Fault is a plain pass-through of the bench inject tag — a real
   VFD's own fault relay, not the ladder's fail-to-run latch (that is a
   separate, higher-level condition computed in permissives.ld). *)
VAR_INPUT
    RunCmd      : BOOL;
    SpeedCmd    : REAL;
    Dt          : REAL;
    InjectFault : BOOL;
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    Running : BOOL;
    SpeedHz : REAL;
    Amps    : REAL;
    Fault   : BOOL;
END_VAR
VAR
    t1 : TON;
END_VAR
VAR CONSTANT
    RampHzPerS : REAL := 10.0; (* speed ramp rate *)
    FullLoadA  : REAL := 22.0; (* amps at MaxHz, full load *)
    MaxHz      : REAL := 60.0; (* VFD speed ceiling *)
END_VAR
Fault := InjectFault;
t1(IN := RunCmd AND NOT Fault, PT := T#500MS);
Running := t1.Q;
IF Running THEN
    SpeedHz := LIMIT(0.0, SpeedHz + LIMIT(-RampHzPerS * Dt, SpeedCmd - SpeedHz, RampHzPerS * Dt), MaxHz);
ELSE
    SpeedHz := MAX(0.0, SpeedHz - RampHzPerS * Dt);
END_IF;
Amps := (SpeedHz / MaxHz) * (SpeedHz / MaxHz) * FullLoadA;
END_FUNCTION_BLOCK
